docs.title: esMorph
docs.text:
esMorph is a morphological analyzer of Spanish: a Rust core with a Python API. For a word form the analyzer finds its analyses in a dictionary built from Wiktionary - the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features - orders them by probability and builds the forms of the word: conjugation, gender and number.

Early version

Before 1.0 the API may change between 0.x versions; the changes are described in the release notes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Analysis

    Lemma, UD part of speech and features, probability of the analysis; the analysis of a sentence in context, lists of words, lemmatization and documents of the anySeg segmenter without the GIL; own words by a sample word

    Analyzer

  • Universal Dependencies

    Parts of speech, features and lemmas by the UD guidelines and the AnCora conventions; verbs with clitics, numbers, signs and names by rules, colloquial spellings by the standard word, unknown words by their ending

    Word analysis

  • Inflection

    Forms of the lexeme and the form by UD features: conjugation, gender and number

    Inflection

  • Command line

    The esmorph command: lemmas, CoNLL-U, TSV or JSON Lines of text, tokens or CoNLL-U files

    The esmorph command

  • Comparison

    Accuracy, inflection and speed compared with simplemma, spaCy, Stanza, ablaut and verbecc, loading and memory

    Comparison

  • Models

    The context model that chooses the analysis by the sentence and the paradigm model that guesses unknown words

    Models

  • Exceptions

    Built-in Python exceptions and FormNotFoundError for missing forms

    Exceptions

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install esmorph

Prebuilt wheels, building from source and the Rust crate are described on the Installation page.

Project structure
  • crates/esmorph - the Rust core of the analyzer: dictionary format, building, analysis, rules, guessing and inflection
  • crates/esmorph-build - building the dictionary from the export of Wiktionary and the counts of the treebanks
  • crates/esmorph-dict-es - the crate with the dictionary for esmorph on crates.io
  • crates/esmorph-py - the Python module esmorph._esmorph on PyO3
  • python/esmorph - the Python package
  • scripts - exporting Wiktionary and the counts of the treebanks, the conventions of the dictionary, training the context model and the model of unknown words, checking the installed package before publishing and the comparison with other tools
  • data - the tables of closed classes after UD Spanish AnCora, of the symbols of units and of spoken spellings, the weights of the context model and of the model of unknown words
  • docs - MkDocs documentation in English and Spanish
  • tests - tests of the Python package

docs.title: Word analysis
docs.text:
An analysis is an Analysis object returned by the analyze and analyze_many methods of the analyzer: the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features, the probability, the words of the token and the source of the analysis. Analyses are immutable; they can be compared (the probability takes no part in the comparison, so an analysis equals its form from forms()), put into sets and pickled. The forms of a word are given by the forms and inflect methods - see Inflection.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
analysis = morph.analyze("cantaban")[0]
analysis.word, analysis.lemma, analysis.pos, analysis.feats, analysis.words, analysis.source

('cantaban',
 'cantar',
 'VERB',
 {'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '3', 'Tense': 'Imp', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'},
 ('cantaban',),
 'dictionary')

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Type Description word str The word form as the dictionary spells it, with its accents; for a colloquial spelling its standard spelling (trabajado of trabajao); a verb with clitics as written, in lower case; a token of the rules as written, without invisible characters, with combining marks joined to their letters, with - for the hyphens U+2010 and U+2011 and with the letters of a ligature (ﬁ is fi) lemma str The lemma pos str UD part of speech: NOUN, VERB, ADJ, DET, ADP and so on feats dict[str, str] UD features: {"Gender": "Fem", "Number": "Plur"}; a new dictionary each time, changing it does not change the analysis prob float Share of the analysis among the analyses of the word; it sums to 1 over all of them. From analyze_sentence - the score of the context model in the sentence words tuple[str, ...] Words of the token: a verb and its clitics, the words of a contraction (del, al, the older desta), a number and its sign or unit (60%), a unit and its number (km.24), or the word itself; the analysis describes the first of them source str Where the analysis comes from: "dictionary" - the word form is in the dictionary, "clitics" - a verb of the dictionary with clitics, "rule" - an analysis by rule, "guess" - a guessed analysis of an unknown word diminutive_of str \| None The word of which the lemma is a diminutive: casa for casitas; None for other words

docs.title: Parts of speech and features
docs.text:
Parts of speech, features and lemmas follow the Universal Dependencies guidelines and, where they are silent, the conventions of the largest Spanish treebank, UD Spanish AnCora, so the output can be compared with spaCy, Stanza and other UD tools:

  • determiners, pronouns, prepositions and conjunctions have the lemmas and features of AnCora: la is the article el (Definite=Def, PronType=Art) or the pronoun él, se is él with Reflex=Yes, su is DET with Poss=Yes, muy is a form of mucho, and so are their older and spoken spellings, as variants: usté is a form of tú; a demonstrative pronoun with an accent (éste) is a variant of the one without;
  • ser, estar, haber, poder, deber, soler, querer and saber have both AUX and VERB analyses; hay is first of all the verb haber;
  • a participle is a verb with the infinitive as the lemma (VerbForm=Part, Tense=Past) and an adjective with the masculine singular as the lemma (VerbForm=Part without Tense);
  • verbs have no -se in the lemma: quejarse is quejar with the clitic se;
  • older and nonstandard forms of a verb are its variants: trujo is traer, vido is ver, habemos is haber;
  • the conditional and the imperative have no Tense; a proper name has no features, and its lemma has a capital letter: madrid and Madrid are Madrid, PSOE stays PSOE;
  • an adjective in -ísimo is its own lemma with Degree=Abs.

If the part of speech of a word depends on context, the word has both analyses: que is PRON and SCONJ, la is DET and PRON, a participle is VERB and ADJ. Features: gender, number, person, tense, mood, verb form, degree, negation (Polarity=Neg of no), definiteness (Definite), the type of a pronoun or a determiner (PronType), possessiveness (Poss), reflexivity (Reflex), the case of personal pronouns (Case) and whether they follow a preposition (PrepCase), politeness (Polite=Form of usted), the type of a numeral (NumType) and how it is written (NumForm), and the kind of a sign of punctuation (PunctType, PunctSide).

docs.title: Order of analyses
docs.text:
Analyses go from the most probable to the least. prob is the share of an analysis among the analyses of the word, by how often the treebanks UD Spanish AnCora and GSD have it; of the verbs of a form the one AnCora has more often as a verb in all its forms has the larger share where the treebanks have the form itself rarely: vengo is first of all venir, not vengar, while sienta, which they have as sentar more often, is first of all sentar; the form of a verb of less than a fifth of the frequency of the verbs of the form does not go first beside a verb of more than three fifths, even where the treebanks have it first: vengan is first of all venir, and sume is sumar. For a word they have not seen, the shares are equal and the order is a guess by the ending of the word and the most common features; a form of several verbs they have seen in other forms gets shares by the frequency of the verbs and of the features instead (vengamos is first of all the subjunctive of venir). A word goes before its older spelling with other accents: á is first of all a, tambien is también. analyze_sentence orders the same analyses by the sentence.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")][:2]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.99), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.01)]

docs.title: Diminutives
docs.text:
A diminutive keeps its own lemma, as in the treebanks: casitas is a form of casita. diminutive_of gives the word it is a diminutive of, as Wiktionary gives it in the first sense of the word: casita is a diminutive of casa, poquito of poco, ahorita of ahora. A word whose first sense in Wiktionary is its own has none, though Wiktionary also has it as a diminutive: señorita, granito; a word whose first sense is a diminutive keeps it, even if texts mostly use it as a word of its own: patilla is a diminutive of pata. About two thousand nouns, adjectives and adverbs of the dictionary have it.

CodeResult 
[
    morph.analyze(word)[0].diminutive_of
    for word in ("casitas", "poquito", "ahorita", "señorita", "granito")
]

['casa', 'poco', 'ahora', None, None]

docs.title: Words with clitics
docs.text:
A verb with enclitic pronouns is analyzed as its verb: the analysis describes the infinitive, the gerund or the imperative, and words gives the words of the token, as Universal Dependencies has them. In older and literary writing a finite form takes enclitics too, when the accent of the token marks it: díjole is dijo + le, quedéme is quedé + me (the imperative would be quédeme). Since 2010 such a token follows the general rules of accents, so a form stressed on its last syllable loses its accent: a lowercase word that is no word of the dictionary, no other verb with clitics and is such a form with one enclitic is first of all that verb, with guesses of the word after it (quedose is quedó + se, fuime is fui + me), and is_known does not tell it. The enclitic is no te or os, nor nos after the first person, which end nouns more often: anisete and macarenos are nouns. A token that is also an imperative that would take an accent with the enclitic is first of all such a form too: acerqueme is acerqué + me, and then the imperative acerque + me, which the spelling writes acérqueme. del and al also have their two words, as do the contractions of de with a pronoun or a demonstrative in older writing: desta is de + esta. A word of the dictionary is not split: comete is a form of cometer, though a few are mostly verbs with clitics: verse is first of all ver + se, cállate is calla + te, and in a sentence they are always such verbs.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.words, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("dámelo")]

[('dar', 'VERB', ('da', 'me', 'lo'), 'clitics')]

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
Case does not matter for finding a word in the dictionary, though a token with a capital letter may also be a name. A word spelled as in the dictionary gives the analyses of that spelling: publico is not público. A word absent as written may be a verb with clitics (verte is ver + te, not verté); otherwise it is looked for without its accents and with a lost diaeresis, and word shows the spelling of the dictionary; for a verb with clitics word is the token as written, in lower case.

CodeResult 
[morph.analyze(word)[0].word for word in ["CAMIÓN", "camion", "pinguino"]]

['camión', 'camión', 'pingüino']

A lowercase word that the dictionary has not, even without its accents, may be a colloquial or an older spelling of a word of the dictionary. Such a word gets the analyses of that word, and word is its standard spelling. The spellings are:

  • a participle without its d: trabajao is trabajado, sío is sido; its accent is not lost, so perdío is perdido, not perdió;
  • a final -á, -é or -ú for -ad, -ed or -ud: caridá is caridad, virtú is virtud;
  • an aspirated f or h: juerza is fuerza, juevo is huevo, juyendo is huyendo;
  • es for ex before a consonant, as older writing has it: estranjero is extranjero, esplicar is explicar.

A word with a capital letter is no such spelling: Trabajao and Julita are names, not trabajado and fulita.

The dictionary also has spellings of words as they sound and common shortened forms: na and naa are nada, pos is pues, to is todo, mu is muy, güeno is bueno, er is el. They have the analyses of the standard word with its lemma and features, and word is the standard spelling; the context chooses among them and the other words of the same spelling (mu is also an interjection). As words of the dictionary, they are found in any case: Güeno is bueno too. The analyses of all these spellings have source equal to "dictionary", while is_known tells only the spellings of the dictionary: na is known, trabajao is not.

CodeResult 
[
    (analysis.word, analysis.lemma)
    for analysis in (
        morph.analyze(word)[0] for word in ["trabajao", "perdío", "caridá", "juerza", "na", "er"]
    )
]

[('trabajado', 'trabajar'), ('perdido', 'perder'), ('caridad', 'caridad'), ('fuerza', 'fuerza'), ('nada', 'nada'), ('el', 'el')]

docs.title: Tokens out of the dictionary
docs.text:
A token that the dictionary does not have gets the analyses of rules, with source equal to "rule" and word as written:

  • a sign of punctuation is PUNCT with the PunctType of its signs if they are of one kind, and PunctSide for brackets and question and exclamation marks; a symbol such as %, € or ² is SYM;
  • a number in digits is NUM with NumForm=Digit|NumType=Card, a year too, also with a sign, a fraction, a power or spaces between thousands (-5, 37½, 10², 10 000); the lemma drops the periods between thousands (10.000 is 10000); a number with a percent sign, a degree sign or a unit is two words, and the analysis is that of the number (60% is 60 and %, 500cc is 500 and cc, -5ºC is -5 and ºC); a unit of one letter is one only as written (3G is a name), a longer one in any case (5Kg, 8GB);
  • an ordinal number in digits is ADJ with NumForm=Digit|NumType=Ord, its gender and number, and the masculine singular as the lemma: 2.ª is 2.º;
  • a Roman numeral is NUM with NumForm=Roman, less often a name; in lower case it is a numeral only: xii;
  • a token with a capital letter is a name, PROPN, with itself as the lemma: Josep, CiU, W., TV-3;
  • a link, an email, a hashtag or a mention in lower case is SYM: www.aeat.es, #hola;
  • an abbreviation with a period in lower case that the dictionary does not have is a noun with itself as the lemma (fig.), and so is a lowercase letter (b).

A lowercase abbreviation with a period that the dictionary has without the period gets the nouns and the symbols of that word, with source equal to "dictionary": kg. is kg. A unit with its period and a number in one token is two words with these analyses: km.24 is km with the words km. and 24, and only its nouns and symbols count (m.36 is no adjective). A word of the dictionary with a period of another part of speech gets no analyses: come. is a verb with the period of a sentence.

A word with a capital letter that the dictionary knows may be a name too, with its share. An initial (D.) and a word without accents that the dictionary has only with them (Angel, Perez) are mostly names, so their name goes first, while another word with a capital letter is a name less often (Estados, Comisión), so its name usually goes after the analyses of the dictionary. Of the words in capitals, a word of up to four letters is mostly an acronym (ETA, PP), so its name usually goes first, while a longer word and a function word - a preposition, a determiner, a pronoun, a conjunction, an auxiliary - are mostly words of a headline (CAMIONES, EL), so their name usually goes after the analyses of the dictionary. A Roman numeral that the dictionary knows as a word, such as VI, XI or X, is a numeral first. A token with a capital letter that splits as a verb with clitics may be a name too: an imperative without an accent mostly is one (Mandela is first of all PROPN), and so is a finite form without an accent (Vila) but one with se, me or le (Vase, Quedose), while an infinitive, a gerund, an imperative with an accent and a finite form with an accent mostly are verbs (Hacerlo, Déjame, Levantóse). A lowercase word is a name rarely: miró is first of all mirar, Miró a name. An analysis of a rule has no other forms: forms() gives the analysis itself. is_known tells only the words of the dictionary.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.feats, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("10.000")]
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("ETA")]

[('10000', 'NUM', {'NumForm': 'Digit', 'NumType': 'Card'}, 'rule')]
[('ETA', 'PROPN', 0.82), ('eta', 'NOUN', 0.18)]

docs.title: Unknown words
docs.text:
A lowercase word that neither the dictionary nor the rules know gets guessed analyses, with source equal to "guess":

  • a word with a hyphen is analyzed by its last part of an open class or a numeral: palestino-israelíes is a form of palestino-israelí;
  • a word with a known prefix is analyzed by the dictionary word without it, of four letters at least after a prefix of three: supergallos is a form of supergallo, sobreandan of sobreandar;
  • a verb with clitics is analyzed by its guessed gerund, or by its guessed infinitive before se or a clitic of the third person: autogenerarse is autogenerar + se;
  • any other word is analyzed by the forms and inflection of the dictionary words with the same endings of up to five letters, which a model that reads the letters of the word chooses among: it learned from the words of the dictionary how a word of every part of speech and inflection ends, and prefers the features that the treebanks have more often; a word in -ísimo is an adjective of Degree=Abs: esbeltísima is a form of esbeltísimo.

A guessed word has its forms, guessed too: forms() and inflect() work as for a word of the dictionary. is_known stays false for it.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")]
morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")[0].inflect(Tense="Pres", Person="1", Number="Sing")

[('zumbear', 'VERB', 1.0)]
'zumbeo'

docs.title: Analyzer
docs.text:
Analyzer(path=None, *, verify=False, words=None)

Morphological analyzer: for a word form it finds all analyses in a dictionary built from Wiktionary - the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features - and orders them by probability. A token that the dictionary does not have gets the analyses of rules, and an unknown lowercase word is guessed. The dictionary is loaded when the analyzer is created.

Exceptions:

  • FileNotFoundError - the dictionary file does not exist;
  • OSError - the dictionary file cannot be read: no access, the path points to a directory, a pipe or a device;
  • ValueError - the file is not an esMorph dictionary, is of another version of the format (a dictionary built by an earlier release is built again) or is damaged (with verify=True, a deliberately crafted file too), the path has a NUL character, an own word does not follow its sample;
  • TypeError - a path that is neither a string nor PathLike, verify that is not bool, words that is no mapping of strings to strings or pairs of strings.
CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
morph.analyze("hablamos")[0]

Analysis(word='hablamos', lemma='hablar', pos='VERB', feats={'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '1', 'Tense': 'Pres', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'}, prob=0.978261, words=('hablamos',), source='dictionary')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description path str / PathLike None Path to the dictionary file; by default, the dictionary of the package verify bool False Check the whole dictionary, for a file of an untrusted source; takes tens of milliseconds words Mapping[str, str \| tuple[str, str]] None Own words and their samples

The object keeps the absolute dictionary path in path of type Path, read-only. The dictionary file is mapped into memory, so processes with the same file share its memory. While an analyzer exists, the file must not be overwritten in place, but it can be replaced with a new file; on Windows an open file can be neither replaced nor deleted. A dictionary is trusted data, like code: loading rejects a damaged file but not every deliberately crafted one, which may make the analysis fail. A dictionary of an untrusted source is loaded with verify=True: a deliberately crafted file is then rejected with ValueError, and pickle keeps the check.

docs.title: Analyses of a word form
docs.text:
analyze · list[Analysis]

analyze(word)

Analyses of the word form, the most probable first; the probabilities sum to 1. Case does not matter for finding the word in the dictionary, though a token with a capital letter may also be a name, and a word absent as written is looked for without its accents and with a lost diaeresis (spelling). A verb with enclitic pronouns is analyzed as its verb (clitics), a token that the dictionary does not have - a sign, a number, a name - by rules, and an unknown lowercase word is guessed. A token that nothing analyzes - with a space or a control character, a lowercase word without a sample such as qzxw - has no analyses. The model of unknown words is read on the first guessed word, in about a millisecond and a half.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word form

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 3)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")]
[(a.lemma, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")][:1]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.986), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.013), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.0)]
[('zumbear', 'guess')]

docs.title: Analyses of a sentence in context
docs.text:
analyze_sentence · list[list[Analysis]]

analyze_sentence(words)

The analyses of the tokens of a sentence, as analyze gives them, ordered by the context model of the dictionary: the first is the one the model chose by the tokens around, and prob is its score in this sentence. A few rules of Spanish then put another analysis first where only it fits, with the scores of the model kept:

  • an article before a finite verb is the clitic pronoun (no la descubras), and so is la or lo before a plural noun that may be a finite verb (no me la quites, ¿me lo preguntas?), though not after a preposition or a determiner nor before a word whose finite forms are imperatives, and after a preposition la, las and los are the article (de la luthiere);
  • a noun right after a verb that takes a bare infinitive is that infinitive (puede ser, parecía pesar), but not after another verb (perdió poder);
  • pesar of a pesar de is the infinitive, as in the treebanks, while the noun stays elsewhere (con profundo pesar);
  • a form of ser and ir is ir:
    • after a reflexive clitic, unless a predicate follows, and before de if the clitic agrees with the form (se fue, se fue de casa, but me fue muy difícil, me fue de gran ayuda);
    • before a (á in older writing) and its goal, unless a prepositional or an adverbial phrase, an hour or al with an infinitive follows (fue a casa, but fue a partir de 1990, fue al principio, fue a las cinco, fue al ver);
    • before a gerund (fue cayendo);
    • not when the model reads the adverb fuera after a verb, a preposition or an adverb (echó fuera a los intrusos);
  • a word after a clitic, the negation, tú or yo is a verb (que te vayas, no vayas, yo bebo), though not after a preposition (punto de no retorno), nor a capitalized name after no (y no Lima), nor after tú or yo that follows a verb (¿has visto tú cosa igual?); after a clitic so is an adverb, an adjective or a participle (se acerca, te quedas, me visto), and after le, les, la and lo a plural noun that may be a verb (le faltas);
  • a capitalized imperative opening a sentence is no name (Indique si desea), unless the model ranks a noun of the dictionary above it (Sangre de Abel), neither is a verb of tú after ¿ or ¡ before a lowercase word (¿Quieres más?, ¡Eres un ingrato!), nor a verb with clitics opening a sentence that the dictionary has not as a word, unless a finite verb follows, also past no and clitics (Dime, ¿no te parece?, but Mandela dijo, Lucila se había puesto); a capitalized word inside a sentence that the clitics would give an accent it has not is a name (en Mirandola); a verb with clitics before usted is the imperative (perdoneme usted);
  • a word of the dictionary that is mostly a verb with clitics is one (¡Cállate!);
  • a rare verb gives way to a frequent one with the same form, before an infinitive also an auxiliary (aunque vengan is venir, not vengar, no pudimos hablar is poder), unless the model chose a participle (había entrevisto), and no form of tú follows se (se viste is vestir).

The model and the rules read an older or colloquial spelling as the word it stands for: fué as fue, podia as podía, trabajao as trabajado. A word with a capital letter keeps its spelling, as a name does (Ramon), unless it opens the sentence and the dictionary reads it as a word rather than a name (Fué).

The tokens are those of one sentence in order, as analyze takes them: a contraction (del) or a verb with clitics (dámelo) is one token. A sentence of one token is analyzed as analyze, and one longer than 256 tokens by parts of about 256. The model - a small neural network trained on the treebanks UD Spanish AnCora and GSD - is read on the first call, in a couple of milliseconds; the method releases the GIL.

Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Tokens of the sentence: a list, a tuple, a generator

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a string or bytes instead of a collection of tokens, a token that is not a string;
  • ValueError - the dictionary has no context model.
CodeResult 
sentence = morph.analyze_sentence(["Ella", "la", "vio"])
[(analyses[0].lemma, analyses[0].pos) for analyses in sentence]
[analysis.pos for analysis in morph.analyze("la")]

[('él', 'PRON'), ('él', 'PRON'), ('ver', 'VERB')]
['DET', 'PRON', 'DET', 'NOUN']

docs.title: Analysis of a document
docs.text:
annotate · anyseg.Document

annotate(document, *, context=True)

Fills the columns lemma, upos and feats of the words of a document of the anySeg segmenter with the most probable analysis of every word in the context of its sentence, as analyze_sentence orders the analyses of its tokens, and returns the document; with context=False, as analyze orders them, about seven times faster. The earlier values of these columns are replaced. A token that the segmenter leaves as one word and whose analysis has several gets these words: pónganselo becomes the multiword token pongan + se + lo, the imperative of poner and two pronouns. The method then returns a new document with these words, while the given one is filled too, such a token with the analysis of the whole. A document whose words cannot change (it has heads, enhanced dependencies or empty nodes) keeps its words, and so does a token whose word has XPOS or MISC other than the spaces after a token, which other words would lose, as in a document read from CoNLL-U; such a token gets the analysis of the whole. A number with a unit stays one word, as in the treebanks: 48km. The words of a multiword token are analyzed by the token: dime split into di + me is the imperative of decir with the pronoun me, and clitics after a verb are pronouns. A word without analyses gets its lower case as the lemma and the part of speech X. The method releases the GIL. esMorph does not depend on anySeg: the document is an anyseg.Document or an object with the same column("form"), multiword_tokens (a token has text and words, a word has index), sentences (a sentence has words) and set_columns; an object without sentences is one sentence, and with context=False they are not read; an object without with_words keeps its words.

Parameter Type Default Description document anyseg.Document - Document of the segmenter (pip install anyseg) context bool True Order the analyses by the context model

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the words of the multiword tokens are not consecutive words of the document in order, the first words of the sentences are not words of the document in order, the analysis is in context and the dictionary has no context model;
  • TypeError - an object that is not a document, a form or the text of a token that is not a string, a token without text or words, a word without index or with an index that is not an integer.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

document = morph.annotate(Segmenter("es").segment("Pónganselo ya."))
[(word.form, word.lemma, word.upos) for word in document.words]
document = Segmenter("es").segment("Ella la vio.")
morph.annotate(document, context=False).words[1].upos
morph.annotate(document).words[1].upos

[('Pongan', 'poner', 'VERB'), ('se', 'él', 'PRON'), ('lo', 'él', 'PRON'), ('ya', 'ya', 'ADV'), ('.', '.', 'PUNCT')]
'DET'
'PRON'

docs.text:
is_known · bool

is_known(word)

Whether the dictionary has the word form, as written or as a verb of the dictionary with clitics; as with analyze, case and lost accents do not matter. Tokens analyzed by rules, guessed words, colloquial spellings that only rules read as words of the dictionary (trabajao, Word analysis) and a finite form with an enclitic without an accent (quedose, Word analysis) are not in the dictionary.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word form

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a word that is not a string.

(True, False)

docs.title: Dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary of the package is built from the English Wiktionary of October 2026 with the words and forms that only the Spanish Wiktionary of November 2026 has: 717 thousand word forms of 136 thousand lexemes. The Spanish edition adds nouns, adjectives, adverbs and interjections and new forms of the words of the English one, but no names and no new verbs; its word gives way to a colloquial or an older spelling of a word of the English edition (juera is fuera, espectativa is expectativa) and to a verb with clitics (abrázala is abraza + la), and with a capital letter it is mostly a name (Navas). Symbols of units (km, kg) come from a table of their own, and determiners, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions and numerals in words from a table after the treebank UD Spanish AnCora, whose conventions the lemmas and features follow (Word analysis). The probabilities of analyses come from the training parts of UD Spanish AnCora and UD Spanish GSD; word forms they do not have get their order by their ending and the most common features. The dictionary is distributed under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

The property dictionary_info describes the dictionary of the analyzer: the source and its main snapshot with its SHA-256, the snapshots of all its sources with theirs (snapshots), the license, the release of Universal Dependencies and the treebanks of the probabilities with their licenses, for a dictionary with a context model the release and the treebanks of its training (context), for a dictionary with a model of unknown words the snapshots and the number of the dictionary words it learned from (paradigms), the number of word forms and the checksum of the file. Every access returns a new dict; its type for type checkers is esmorph.DictionaryInfo, of context - esmorph.ContextInfo, and of paradigms - esmorph.ParadigmsInfo.

CodeResult 
info = morph.dictionary_info
info["source"], info["license"], sorted(info["treebanks"])

('Wiktionary', 'CC BY-SA 4.0', ['UD_Spanish-AnCora', 'UD_Spanish-GSD'])

docs.title: Own words
docs.text:
The parameter words adds words that the dictionary does not have. Each word comes with its sample: a word of the dictionary in the same form, usually the lemma.

  • The word takes the forms of the lexemes of its sample with their features, order and shares: {"tiktokear": "bloguear"} gives tiktokeo, tiktokeó and tiktokeando.
  • A sample with lexemes of several parts of speech needs the part of speech, a UD tag in capitals, in a pair: {"zajo": ("bajo", "NOUN")}; the pair may be a list, and several parts of speech are separated by commas: {"tiktokero": ("bloguero", "ADJ,NOUN")}. An empty part of speech is none.
  • The word takes the endings of its sample, so the sample is a word of the same part of speech with the same ending: {"marramiau": ("miau", "INTJ")}, {"Wolfsburgo": ("Hamburgo", "PROPN")}.
  • A sample may be an own word given earlier: {"tiktokear": "bloguear", "feisbuquear": "tiktokear"}.
  • An own word may have letters that the dictionary has not.
  • A word of the dictionary given as an own word keeps its analyses, and the new ones join them.
  • The analyses of own words are those of words of the dictionary, with source equal to "dictionary", and they are inflected like their samples.
CodeResult 
own = Analyzer(words={"tiktokear": "bloguear", "zajo": ("bajo", "NOUN")})
[
    (analysis.lemma, analysis.pos)
    for analysis in (own.analyze(word)[0] for word in ["tiktokeó", "zajos"])
]

[('tiktokear', 'VERB'), ('zajo', 'NOUN')]

A sample that is not in the dictionary, a sample with lexemes of several parts of speech without one, a part of speech that the sample has not (("bajo", "noun")), a word without the ending of its sample ("tiuteo" as "bloguear") and a word with a space raise ValueError. The analyzer shares the dictionary mapped into memory with the analyzers of the same file. Twenty thousand own words are added in a twentieth to a third of a second (verbs take the longest), and the analysis is a few percent slower. Every analyzer keeps its own words in memory: twenty thousand words of the treebanks take about 4 MB, twenty thousand verbs about 2 MB. Adding them needs up to about 35 MB more for a moment, which the process may keep for later use, so a process with one such analyzer grows by 10-40 MB. Pickle keeps the own words, and a process that unpickles an analyzer with own words or its analyses many times, as a worker of a pool does, makes the analyzer once and keeps the last two such analyzers until the process ends. The command takes own words from a file with -w.

docs.title: Threads and processes
docs.text:
One analyzer can be used from several threads. lemmatize, analyze_sentence and annotate release the GIL, so threads speed them up. analyze_many creates the analyses as Python objects, so threads speed it up little on any Python, the free-threaded one (3.14t, 3.15t) included: for a large text, lemmatize or processes are faster. The analyzer and analyses are pickled, so they work with multiprocessing and joblib: processes share the dictionary mapped into memory. Pickling an analysis costs more than finding it, so workers that return lemmas or tuples of fields are faster than workers that return analyses. A pickle keeps the absolute path of the dictionary file (none for the dictionary of the package) and the place of the analysis in the tables of that dictionary, which is looked up anew only with another dictionary: unpickling loads each dictionary once per process, so analyses unpickled one by one share one analyzer, an analysis whose dictionary file is gone or of another version of the format takes the dictionary of the package, and a damaged file raises ValueError. An analysis that the dictionary does not have, as one pickled with another version of it, keeps its fields, but forms() gives an empty list and inflect raises FormNotFoundError.

CodeResult 
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

texts = [["los", "niños", "cantaban"], ["el", "gato", "come"]]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
    lemmas = list(pool.map(morph.lemmatize, texts))
lemmas

[['el', 'niño', 'cantar'], ['el', 'gato', 'comer']]

docs.title: The esmorph command
docs.text:
esmorph [options] [file ...]

The command analyzes text from files or the standard input and writes lemmas, parts of speech and Universal Dependencies features in one of four formats. It is installed with the package (pip install esmorph) and also runs as python -m esmorph; without Python, cargo install esmorph --features cli installs it. Every word gets its most probable analysis in the context of its sentence, as annotate gives it: the words of a multiword token are analyzed by the token. The Rust core analyzes and writes in one thread, about 190 thousand tokens per second, and 1.6 million with --no-context.

echo "Dime la verdad del caso." | esmorph

decir yo el verdad de el caso .

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description -f, --format lemmas Output format: lemmas, conllu, tsv, jsonl -i, --input text Input: text, tokens, conllu -d, --dictionary the package dictionary An esMorph dictionary file, checked whole as with verify=True -w, --words A file of own words: per line a word and its sample separated by a tab, and the part of speech if the sample has lexemes of several (several are separated by commas: ADJ,NOUN); the option may repeat --no-context Order the analyses of a word as analyze does, without the context model: faster; for a list of words and a dictionary without a context model -o, --output the standard output The result file; - is the standard output -h, --help Show the help -V, --version Show the version

Files are read one after another; without files and in place of - the standard input is read. The input is in UTF-8: a file in another encoding (Latin-1, cp1252, UTF-16) is not analyzed, unless its first letter with an accent comes after the first 64 KiB: then the text before that line is analyzed up to its last blank line. A single line with invalid bytes is analyzed with U+FFFD in their place. An option value is written separately or attached: -f conllu, -fconllu, --format=conllu. Text is analyzed by paragraphs: a paragraph is written as soon as a blank line or the end of the input closes it - on a terminal at once, and to a pipe or a file whenever the command waits for the next input line, so it can be kept open and fed text paragraph by paragraph. The inputs tokens and conllu are written by sentences.

A file of own words is in UTF-8; blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, and spaces around a field are ignored:

# new verbs
tiktokear   bloguear
zajo    bajo    NOUN

With it, esmorph -w words.tsv text.txt analyzes tiktokeó as a form of tiktokear, as Analyzer(words=...) does.

In Windows PowerShell 5.1 the > redirection and a pipeline (Get-Content text.txt | esmorph) corrupt letters with accents: pass the file as an argument and write the result with the -o option (in PowerShell 7 they work too). Text passed with echo in cmd comes in the console encoding: run chcp 65001 first.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• text - text: a blank line ends a paragraph. Tokens, their words and sentences are found by the segmenter anySeg following the conventions of Universal Dependencies: del and al are two words, and so are an infinitive or a gerund with clitics (dárselo) and frequent imperatives (dime). A token that the segmenter leaves as one word and whose analysis has several gets these words: devuélvenos is devuelve + nos, the imperative of devolver and a pronoun. A paragraph longer than 256 KiB is analyzed in pieces that end at a sentence boundary, so memory does not grow with the length of the input; its sentences may then differ slightly from those of the whole text.
  • tokens - one token per line, a blank line separates sentences; separators around the token and everything after a tab are ignored, so a table with the token in the first column works too. A token gets the words of its analysis: dime is di + me. A sentence without a blank line is closed after 8,192 tokens. The words around a token change its analysis, so a list of words that do not make a sentence is analyzed with --no-context or with a blank line after every word; the tsv format gives a line per word.
  • conllu - CoNLL-U: the LEMMA, UPOS and FEATS columns are filled, while the other columns, comments, multiword tokens and empty nodes stay as they are. A token of one word whose analysis has several gets these words, unless its sentence has heads, enhanced dependencies or empty nodes or its word has XPOS or MISC other than the spaces after a token, which new words would lose. An invalid sentence is written as it is in the conllu format and left out of the others, its line goes to the error message, and the rest of the file is analyzed.
printf '1\tCasas\t_\t_\t_\t_\t0\troot\t_\t_\n2\tblancas\t_\t_\t_\t_\t1\tamod\t_\t_\n' | esmorph -i conllu -f conllu

1   Casas   casa    NOUN    _   Gender=Fem|Number=Plur  0   root    _   _
2   blancas blanco  ADJ _   Gender=Fem|Number=Plur  1   amod    _   _

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: All formats except jsonl give every word its most probable analysis; jsonl writes all analyses of every token, the most probable first. A word without analyses gets its lower case as the lemma and the part of speech X.

docs.title: lemmas
docs.text: The lemmas of the words of a sentence separated by spaces, a line per sentence; for the text input paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

docs.title: conllu
docs.text:
CoNLL-U as anySeg writes it: multiword tokens with their words, the sent_id and text comments and, for the text input, newdoc at the start of a file, newpar at the start of a paragraph, SpaceAfter=No and SpacesAfter in MISC. The result is the same as annotate of the whole text, except for paragraphs longer than 256 KiB. Analysis gives no syntax tree: from the text and tokens inputs the HEAD and DEPREL columns are _, so a tool that needs a tree, such as the evaluation script of the CoNLL 2018 shared task, reads the result of -i conllu on a file that has one.

echo "Dímelo del mar." | esmorph -f conllu

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code When 0 Success, including when the output is closed before the end (esmorph text.txt \| head) 1 An input file is missing, cannot be read or is not in UTF-8, a line is not in UTF-8 (it is analyzed with U+FFFD), an invalid CoNLL-U sentence; the rest is still analyzed 1 The dictionary cannot be read or is damaged, it has no context model and --no-context is not given, a file of own words cannot be read or has a wrong line (the message gives the file and the line), the output file cannot be created, the output file or the standard output is an input file, the dictionary or a file of own words; nothing is analyzed 1 A write error, a closed standard output (the command installed with cargo writes it to /dev/null and ends with 0); the analysis stops 2 Invalid options

Error messages go to the standard error.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: esMorph gives all the analyses of a word, the most probable first, and orders them by the sentence with its context model. In context its first analysis has the right part of speech, features and lemma all together for 95.82 % of the words of AnCora, almost as often as spaCy es_core_news_sm trained on it (95.85 %), and more often than spaCy and Stanza on PUD and COSER, new to all of them; its lemma is right more often than that of every other system on AnCora and COSER. Without context its first lemma is right more often than that of simplemma on all three UD test sets, and an analysis with the right part of speech and lemma is among its analyses for 97-99 % of words. It conjugates verbs more accurately than ablaut and verbecc. It analyzes 196 thousand tokens per second in context, 4.0 times faster than spaCy, and 1.8 million without, answers a short text together with loading in 3.4 ms, and every further process with the same dictionary adds 5.8 MB of memory.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
The gold standard is the test parts of the UD Spanish AnCora, GSD, PUD and COSER treebanks from the UD 2.19 release: news, web texts, translated Wikipedia sentences and rural speech. Every system gets their words, with del as de and el and a verb apart from its clitics, and esMorph in context gets the tokens of a sentence, a multiword token with its words, as annotate takes a document; punctuation is not counted, and lemmas are compared ignoring case. The lemmas and features of GSD are assigned automatically, so only the part of speech is compared on it. The treebanks follow different conventions, so systems should be compared on the same set rather than sets against each other.

AnCora is the home set of the taggers and of esMorph: spaCy es_core_news_sm is trained on AnCora, the default Stanza model on AnCora and GSD, and esMorph takes its conventions, the frequencies of its analyses and its context model from the training parts of AnCora and GSD. PUD and COSER are new to all of them.

docs.title: Lemma
docs.text:
The share of words with the right lemma, %; for esMorph - the lemma of the first analysis, for a word without analyses - the word in lower case, as lemmatize gives it, and in context - the lemma of the analysis that annotate chooses:

System AnCora PUD COSER esMorph 97.83 97.69 94.92 esMorph in context 99.32 97.71 96.81 simplemma 96.96 96.96 93.50 spaCy es_core_news_sm 98.61 96.69 93.39 Stanza 99.20 97.80 94.98

simplemma gives only a lemma, from a dictionary without parts of speech.

docs.title: Part of speech and features
docs.text:
Taggers and esMorph in context choose the analysis by the sentence; without context the first analysis of esMorph for a word such as que, la or como is the most frequent one. On PUD the features without context are right a little more often than in context: the context model learns the conventions of AnCora, and PUD tags the words of names and participles otherwise.

The share of words with the right part of speech, features (gender, number, person, tense, mood, verb form; for names and numerals they are not compared, PUD gives them a gender and a number) and all together with the lemma, %; for esMorph - the first analysis, and the oracle - at least one of its analyses has the right part of speech and lemma:

docs.title: Inflection
docs.text:
The share of verbs whose form the system gives for their gold lemma and features (infinitive, gerund, participle, mood, tense, person and number), %. Every system gets only the lemma and the features: esMorph is scored by inflect of its verb and auxiliary lexemes of the lemma, one form of each, ablaut and verbecc by any form of the cell of their conjugation table:

System AnCora PUD COSER esMorph 99.66 93.29 95.47 ablaut 98.89 92.71 93.61 verbecc 95.39 92.91 93.53

On AnCora most misses of ablaut and verbecc are the third person singular of the present of haber: ablaut gives only ha and verbecc only hay, while esMorph has both, ha of the auxiliary and hay of the verb; verbecc also fails on pasar, resultar and suceder, which count as misses. On PUD most misses of all three are a convention: the auxiliaries ha and había of compound tenses have Tense=Past; COSER has spoken forms such as trabajao and tá. For the imperfect subjunctive esMorph and ablaut give the form in -ra (fuera), so a form in -se (fuese) is a miss for them.

docs.title: Text analysis
docs.text:
The time to analyze a text together with importing and loading the system in a new process, seconds, both axes on a logarithmic scale:

On a short text almost all the time goes to loading: esMorph answers in 3.4 ms and in 5.6 ms in context, simplemma in 0.31 s, spaCy in 0.82 s, Stanza in 1.7 s. On a long text the analysis speed decides, tokens per second without loading, more is better:

System Tokens per second simplemma, lemmas only 2,693,270 esMorph 1,778,677 esMorph in context 196,159 spaCy es_core_news_sm 49,381 Stanza 3,092

esMorph gives all the analyses of a word, with features and probabilities; its lemmatization alone is almost as fast as simplemma, see Operations.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Thousands of words, analyses or tables per second, more is better:

Operation esMorph simplemma ablaut verbecc Analysis of a word form: analyze in a loop 1,214 - - - Analysis of a list: analyze_many 1,691 - - - Analysis of sentences in context: analyze_sentence, tokens 169 - - - Lemmatization: lemmatize, lemmatize(word, lang="es") 2,007 2,116 - - Lemmatization in 4 threads: lemmatize 6,707 - - - Form of a noun or an adjective: inflect(Number="Plur") 1,609 - - - Form of a verb: inflect(Mood="Sub", Tense="Pres", Person="1", Number="Sing") 591 - - - Conjugation table: forms(), conjugate(lemma) 113 - 1.7 0.9

simplemma keeps its answers in a cache: with the cache filled by an earlier run over the same words it lemmatizes 5.5 million words per second. ablaut and verbecc build a form only as part of the whole table. lemmatize releases the GIL, so threads sharing one analyzer run in parallel.

docs.title: Loading and memory
docs.text:
esMorph simplemma spaCy es_core_news_sm Stanza Import and loading 3.7 ms 0.33 s 0.96 s 1.9 s Growth of process memory 12.4 MB 131 MB 305 MB 578 MB Every further process 5.8 MB 129 MB 359 MB 1.6 GB

The dictionary file of esMorph is mapped into memory, so multiprocessing or joblib processes and web server workers share it: most of the 12.4 MB of the first process is the dictionary, and every further process adds only its own tables, models and analyses. The context model is read on the first analysis of a sentence: about 2 ms and 4 MB more; the model of unknown words on the first guessed word: about 1.5 ms and 1.4 MB more.

docs.title: How it was measured
docs.text:
• Quality, inflection and text analysis - the scripts/compare.py script: uv run scripts/compare.py target/compare --chart docs/img/speed.svg. It installs the systems into a separate environment with the versions of all packages pinned in scripts/compare.py.lock (esMorph - the version from it, or a wheel with uv run --with dist/esmorph-*.whl, as for this page), downloads the treebank test parts and the Stanza model with checksum verification before measuring and analyzes the gold words; esMorph in context annotates a document of the gold tokens, with the words of the multiword tokens and the gold sentences. Inflection - the 5,967, 2,893 and 1,237 verbs of AnCora, PUD and COSER whose lemma is an infinitive, without typos and foreign words.
  • Versions: Python 3.11, esMorph 0.6.0, simplemma 2.0.0, spaCy 3.8.16 with the es_core_news_sm 3.8.0 model without the parser and NER, Stanza 1.15.0 with the default model on the CPU (torch 2.15.0), ablaut 0.11.0, verbecc 2.0.3 (the package has no model and trains one at the first run, so its figures vary by up to 0.2 between installations). Computer - Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26, with other applications running (load average 3-4), so the speeds are an order of magnitude.
  • Text analysis speed - the 53,622 tokens of the AnCora test part with punctuation: tokens per second - the best of two analyses of the whole part after loading, chart points - the best of three runs of importing, loading and analyzing the first 10-50,000 tokens in a new process. Only the call of the system is measured: esMorph analyze_many of all the words and in context annotate of the document, simplemma lemmatize of each word with an empty cache, spaCy nlp.pipe of the sentences, Stanza the whole text; esMorph and simplemma run in one thread, spaCy and Stanza with their default settings.
  • Operations - 47,288 words of the AnCora test part without punctuation, for analyze_sentence its 1,721 sentences of 52,454 tokens with punctuation, a multiword token as one token; the best of three runs in one thread, except the row with threads; verbs - the lexemes of the 4,663 gold verbs whose lemma is an infinitive (verbecc - the first 2,000, one run). Loading and memory - importing, creating the analyzer and the first analysis, the growth of the resident memory of the process (ps -o rss), the median of six runs (of seven for esMorph); a further process - the growth of the memory the process does not share with others (USS), in each of four multiprocessing processes that load the system and analyze 200 sentences.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
The library raises built-in Python exceptions and one of its own, FormNotFoundError, a subclass of LookupError. It is available from esmorph.

Exception Built-in class When it is raised FormNotFoundError LookupError The lexeme has no form with the requested features, or the dictionary has no lexeme of the analysis (inflect) ValueError - The feature or the value is not in the dictionary (inflect); the file is not an esMorph dictionary, is of another version of the format (a dictionary built by an earlier release is built again) or is damaged, with verify=True a deliberately crafted file too, the path has a NUL character, an own word does not follow its sample (Analyzer); the dictionary has no context model or its model is damaged (analyze_sentence, annotate in context); the words of the multiword tokens are not consecutive words of the document in order, the first words of the sentences are not words of the document in order (annotate) TypeError - An argument of the wrong type: a word or a feature value that is not a string, a string or bytes instead of a collection of words (analyze_many, analyze_sentence, lemmatize), a dictionary path that is neither a string nor PathLike, verify that is not bool, words that is no mapping of strings to strings or pairs of strings (Analyzer); an object that is not a document, a form or the text of a token that is not a string, the index of a word that is not an integer, a sentence without words (annotate) FileNotFoundError OSError The dictionary file does not exist (Analyzer) PermissionError, IsADirectoryError and others OSError The dictionary file cannot be read or is not a file (Analyzer)

Exception messages are in English.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer, FormNotFoundError

morph = Analyzer()
try:
    morph.analyze("casa")[0].inflect(Gender="Masc")
except FormNotFoundError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, isinstance(e, LookupError))
try:
    morph.analyze("gato")[0].inflect(Number="Plural")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)

FormNotFoundError True
Unknown value of the feature Number: Plural; the dictionary has Plur, Sing

docs.title: Inflection
docs.text: Every analysis knows its lexeme - the forms of the word with the same lemma and part of speech. forms() gives all of them, and inflect() gives the form with the given Universal Dependencies features. The lexeme follows the conventions of the analyses: the auxiliary haber and the verb haber are two lexemes, and so are a participle and the adjective it makes.

docs.title: Forms of the lexeme
docs.text:
forms() returns the forms as analyses like those of analyze, with prob equal to 1. The lemma goes first, then the paradigm: for a verb the infinitive, the gerund, the participles and the finite forms by mood (indicative, conditional, subjunctive, imperative), tense, number and person; for a noun or an adjective by number and gender. Variants - the forms of vos, old and regional spellings - follow the paradigm. An analysis equals its form from forms(): the probability takes no part in the comparison.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
[form.word for form in morph.analyze("bonitas")[0].forms()]
[form.word for form in morph.analyze("hablamos")[0].forms()][:12]

['bonito', 'bonita', 'bonitos', 'bonitas']
['hablar', 'hablando', 'hablado', 'hablada', 'hablados', 'habladas', 'hablo', 'hablas', 'habla', 'hablamos', 'habláis', 'hablan']

docs.title: Form by features
docs.text:
inflect(**feats) returns the form with the given features as a string. The features that are not given are kept where possible: gatos in the singular is gato, in the feminine gatas. An infinitive or a gerund asked for a tense, a mood, a person or a number gives a finite form.

CodeResult 
gatos = morph.analyze("gatos")[0]
gatos.inflect(Number="Sing"), gatos.inflect(Gender="Fem")
morph.analyze("hablar")[0].inflect(Tense="Past", Person="3", Number="Plur")

('gato', 'gatas')
'hablaron'

Several forms may have the same features. A variant comes only from a variant: hablás in the imperative is hablá, while hablas is habla; an old or nonstandard form comes only from such a form: trujo in the plural is trujeron, while podés is podéis. A variant of a noun, an adjective, a determiner or a pronoun still gives a main form closer in spelling than its variants: buen in the plural is buenos, not the older bones. Of the two forms of the imperfect subjunctive the analysis keeps its own: hablase in the first person plural is hablásemos. Otherwise a form that the treebanks have clearly more often goes first (the verb haber gives hay, the auxiliary gives ha), and the order of the table of the word decides the rest: ser gives soy, not seigo. A form of some countries only is a variant: the feminine participle of apagar is apagada, not apaga.

CodeResult 
[(a.pos, a.inflect(Person="3", Number="Sing")) for a in morph.analyze("haber")[:2]]

[('AUX', 'ha'), ('VERB', 'hay')]

A form of a noun, a name, an adjective, a determiner, a pronoun or a numeral without a gender or a number agrees with any: grande in the feminine plural is grandes, and an analysis of a rule stays itself (ETA). Of the forms that keep equally many features of the analysis, a form that changes another feature goes after one that lacks it, and a form with the gender and number of the analysis before one without them: chulitos in the singular is chulito, lo in the dative is le, sí in the dative is se, a clitic gives a clitic (le in the accusative is lo, not él), and ustedes, which has no gender, stays ustedes in the feminine. A value with several parts, such as Case=Acc,Nom, may be given in any order. A verb with clitics inflects as its verb, and its forms have no clitics: dámelo in the plural is dad.

CodeResult 
grande, token = morph.analyze("grande")[0], morph.analyze("dámelo")[0]
grande.inflect(Gender="Fem", Number="Plur"), token.inflect(Number="Plur")

('grandes', 'dad')

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
• FormNotFoundError, a subclass of LookupError - the lexeme has no form with these features: casa has no masculine; or the dictionary has no lexeme of the analysis, as one pickled with another version of it;
  • ValueError - the dictionary has no such feature or value, as in Number="Plural"; the message lists the valid ones;
  • TypeError - a value is not a string.
CodeResult 
from esmorph import FormNotFoundError

try:
    morph.analyze("casa")[0].inflect(Gender="Masc")
except FormNotFoundError as error:
    print(error)

The lexeme of 'casa' has no form Gender=Masc

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install esmorph

The package also installs the esmorph command.

docs.title: Prebuilt wheels
docs.text:
PyPI hosts wheels for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, manylinux and musllinux), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64 and arm64). One wheel serves every Python version starting with 3.11, and the free-threaded Python 3.14t and 3.15t have wheels of their own; Rust is not needed to install them. The dictionary is part of the package and needs no separate installation. The free-threaded Python 3.13 is not supported: free-threaded builds start with 3.14.

Pre-release versions X.Y.Z.devN are published only on TestPyPI:

pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ --pre esmorph

uv takes a package from the first index that has it, so it needs another order of indexes:

uv pip install --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --pre esmorph

docs.title: Building from source
docs.text:
On other platforms and on free-threaded builds newer than 3.15 pip builds the package from source, which requires Rust 1.88 or newer:

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
pip install esmorph

The development environment is described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
The analyzer core is published on crates.io as the esmorph crate and the dictionary as the esmorph-dict-es crate: it is enabled by default through the feature bundled and loaded with Dictionary::bundled(). The API documentation is on docs.rs.

cargo add esmorph

The feature anyseg adds Dictionary::annotate for documents of the segmenter anySeg, and the feature cli adds the esmorph command, which installs without Python:

cargo install esmorph --features cli

docs.title: Models
docs.text: esMorph finds the analyses of a word in its dictionary and uses two small neural networks: the context model chooses the analysis of a word by its sentence, and the paradigm model guesses the analyses of a word that the dictionary does not have. Both run in the Rust core without other libraries, and their weights are sections of the dictionary file.

docs.title: Context model
docs.text:
A word such as vino is a noun or a verb, la an article or a pronoun, como a conjunction or a verb. Without context the dictionary orders the analyses of a word by how often the treebanks UD Spanish AnCora and GSD have them; analyze_sentence, annotate and the command order them by the sentence:

For every token the model reads its shape (case, digits, the start of the sentence), the word, its endings and the analyses the dictionary gives it; a bidirectional LSTM reads the tokens of the sentence in both directions, and every analysis of a token gets a score by the vector of its token, its tags and its source. The probabilities of the analyses of a token are the softmax of the scores. A few rules of Spanish then put another analysis first where only it fits (analyze_sentence).

The model learned on the training parts of AnCora (all the features and the lemma) and GSD (only the part of speech, brought to the conventions of AnCora), and the epoch was chosen on the development part of AnCora.

docs.title: Paradigm model
docs.text:
A lowercase word that the dictionary does not have is guessed by the words of the dictionary with the same endings: their forms and inflection tables are its candidates. The model reads the letters of the word from its end and scores every candidate by its tag, the suffixes of its lemma and of its form, the length of its ending and how many words of the dictionary have it. It learned from the words of the dictionary itself, each guessed as if the dictionary did not have it, and prefers the features that the treebanks have more often.

The frequency of an ending alone prefers what most words with it are; the model also reads the rest of the word:
